verdict.rationale: Maritime documents a CLI designed for other AI agents to operate non-interactively (JSON output, env-var auth), idempotent SDK provisioning of VM-backed agents, and per-user Linux computers a model can drive. That covers provisioning and agent-driven operation of an isolated environment. The rest of the loop is weak or absent: there is no explicit code-execution endpoint, results can only be read indirectly through the Files API, and teardown is not documented. missing for 10: a documented exec/run-code call with returned output, a documented teardown/delete operation, an end-to-end agent-run lifecycle example, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: The Maritime CLI is built to be operated by other AI agents, not just humans: machine-readable output on every command, stable exit codes, and a live self-describing contract.
Authenticate with an env var, never interactively.
`provision` is **idempotent** on it: it returns the existing agent if there is one, else creates a new one.
Agents are getting a real Linux desktop they can drive: screenshot, mouse, keyboard, and a live view you can take over.
eight endpoints and both SDKs to browse, upload, download, and edit an agent's disk over HTTP, even while the agent sleeps.
